description: Brazilian insurtech MGA selling individual life insurance through 11,000 broker partners, backed by risk-carrier Excelsior. 100K policies active, R$307M in annualized premiums, 1% share of a R$25B market dominated by Bradesco and Prudential (64% combined).
current_status: Post-Series C deploying capital into AI underwriting and claims. Targeting 'the Nubank of life insurance' positioning. No reserve capital requirements (MGA model), 97 employees, 11K brokers active.

founder.name: Rafael Cló
founder.background: Stanford MBA. Personal pain trigger: couldn't reinstate his own life-insurance policy after a credit-card expiry — became the founding insight.
founder.problem_fit: HIGH on the UX and GTM layer (the friction he personally experienced). LOW on the hard layers: life-insurance underwriting, SUSEP regulatory navigation, actuarial pricing — all delegated to partner Excelsior.
founder.execution_evidence: Built Azos to 100K policies and R$307M annualized premiums via broker network; closed Series C. Has not yet demonstrated operating the regulated layer himself.
founder.red_flags: First-time founder in a heavily regulated industry (insurance) without a regulatory co-founder. MGA dependency is the structural consequence of this founder profile.

stage_context.vs_base: Azos outperforms Series C base rate in thriving (+6pp) driven by TAM expansion (insurance penetration 2.4% of GDP in Brazil vs 7%+ Chile) and AI underwriting edge. Breakout (±0pp) — capped by MGA dependency: the largest outcomes require balance-sheet ownership, which Azos does not have.

verdict: Azos survives 18 months IF (a) churn stays below 7%/month on policies (life insurance benchmark is 1-2%), (b) Selic cuts reach 200bp+ by Q4 2026 enabling middle-class insurance uptake, (c) Excelsior does not renegotiate MGA economics as Azos scales. Most fragile: (c) — Azos has zero publicly-documented contractual leverage over its risk carrier.
top_risk: MGA dependency: if Excelsior demands a larger risk share or exits, Azos has no life-insurance license and no alternative carrier lined up publicly
top_opportunity: Loss-frame GTM via Cialdini-style local testimonials — Brazilian middle class responds 3-5x stronger to peer social proof than Bradesco's institutional branding
